## 13. Worker Concurrency & Isolation — Missing Infrastructure

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Design references**: `WORKER_INFRASTRUCTURE.md` §1 (architecture), §7.3 (port forwarding), §8 (GCS repo snapshots), §11.2 (desktop worktrees), `ONTOLOGY_COW.md` (DB-level COW)  
**Priority**: HIGH — blocks horizontal scaling of task throughput per worker

### Current State

Workers register with `max_concurrent_tasks: 1` (hardcoded in `g5d/src/worker/mod.rs`). The poll/execute loop is sequential: poll → execute → reset → poll. A single `current_task_id: Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>` tracks the active task. Parallelism today comes from running **3 worker replicas** (separate OS processes via docker-compose `deploy.replicas: 3`), not from in-process concurrency.

This is fine for the current prototype stage but limits throughput: each worker process consumes a full pod's resources even when idle between tasks, and the 1:1 model means scaling to N concurrent tasks requires N pods (N × 4–8 CPU, N × 8–16 GiB RAM).

### 13.1 COW Workspace Snapshots (filesystem layer)

**Problem**: Each concurrent task needs its own writable view of the workspace files. Today `build_and_execute_task()` uses a single `workspace_path` (either `config.workspace_path` or the `workspace_git_url` repo dir) — all tasks share the same directory. This is why `max_concurrent_tasks` is hardcoded to `1`: two tasks writing to the same checkout would corrupt each other.

**Designed model** (WORKER_INFRASTRUCTURE.md §1, §8, §11.2):

| Mode | COW mechanism | How it works |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| **Cloud (krunvm)** | virtio-fs + overlayfs inside guest | The host pulls the workspace once. Each microVM mounts the host directory read-only via virtio-fs. An overlayfs inside the guest provides a private writable layer. Writes stay in the guest overlay; the host base is untouched. |
| **Desktop** | git worktree per task | `git worktree add .g5/worktrees/{taskId} -b task/{taskId}` gives each local worker process its own independent checkout sharing the same `.git` object store. |

**The krunvm backend already mounts the host dir via virtio-fs** (`MicrovmRunSpec.mount_host_dir → mount_guest_dir`), but the guest does NOT set up an overlayfs yet — it mounts the virtio-fs share read-write directly, which means two concurrent VMs on the same host would still stomp each other's files.

**What's missing**:

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.1a | **Guest overlayfs init**: On VM boot, set up `overlayfs` with the virtio-fs share as `lowerdir` and a tmpfs/scratch disk as `upperdir`. Agent sees a unified view at `/work`; writes go to the upper layer. | 1.5 days | Add to `g5d vm-exec` entrypoint or base image `init`. Needs `fuse-overlayfs` for rootless. |
| 13.1b | **Desktop worktree lifecycle**: Wire `git worktree add/remove` into `build_and_execute_task()` so each task gets `.g5/worktrees/{taskId}`. Cleanup on complete/fail/cancel. | 1.5 days | The lifecycle manager's `phase_prepare` already has the checkout stubs. |
| 13.1c | **GCS repo snapshots**: Implement `init-workspace.sh` (download `repo_snapshots/<repo>/<commit>.tar.zst` from GCS, fall back to `git clone --depth=1`). | 2 days | Script spec in WORKER_INFRASTRUCTURE.md §8. Only needed for cloud cold start — desktop workers use the existing local clone. |
| 13.1d | **Snapshot build pipeline**: Cloud Build step to produce `.tar.zst` snapshots on push to default branch. | 1 day | Add to `cloudbuild-deploy.yaml`. |

### 13.2 MicroVM Isolation — Same-Host Concurrency (krunvm/libkrun)

**Architecture**: MicroVMs run on the **same host** as the g5d worker process via `krunvm`/`libkrun`. Each task gets its own VM with a separate guest kernel, enforced CPU/RAM caps, and the workspace mounted via virtio-fs. This is how concurrent task execution achieves isolation without requiring separate Kubernetes pods per task.

```
One g5d worker host
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                     │
│  g5d process (orchestrator, poll loop, heartbeat)                  │
│  workspace at /data/repos/{repo_id}  ← pulled once from API       │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐   │
│  │ krunvm (task-1)  │  │ krunvm (task-2)  │  │ krunvm (task-3)  │  │
│  │ guest kernel     │  │ guest kernel     │  │ guest kernel     │  │
│  │ virtio-fs mount  │  │ virtio-fs mount  │  │ virtio-fs mount  │  │
│  │  └─ overlayfs    │  │  └─ overlayfs    │  │  └─ overlayfs    │  │
│  │     lower: /work │  │     lower: /work │  │     lower: /work │  │
│  │     upper: tmpfs │  │     upper: tmpfs │  │     upper: tmpfs │  │
│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘   │
│         ▲                      ▲                      ▲           │
│         └──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┘           │
│                 shared read-only base (host filesystem)            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**What exists in code** (complete, ~2900 LOC in `g5d/src/isolation/`):
- `IsolationManager` — backend selection + lifecycle
- `KrunvmBackend` — boots OCI images via `krunvm` CLI or `libkrun` FFI
- `Wsl2Backend` — krunvm via KVM inside WSL2 kernel
- `ProcessBackend` — explicit process backend on desktop; current fallback
  semantics are tracked debt because they do not provide a safe substitute for
  VM-backed isolation
- `TaskIsolationHandle` — per-task VM handle, `exec_command()` routes into VM
- Runtime detection: `/dev/kvm`, HVF (macOS ARM64), WSL2, `krunvm` binary

**What's missing for same-host concurrency**:

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.2a | **Guest overlayfs** (same as 13.1a — the COW layer lives inside the VM) | — | See 13.1a |
| 13.2b | **Default guest image**: publish a public OCI image with common language runtimes, build tools, `fuse-overlayfs`, and container runtime support for nested-container workloads | 2 days | This is the shared "works out of the box" image that self-hosted customers can trim or extend. |
| 13.2c | **Base image pipeline**: Cloud Build weekly rebuild + security scan | 1 day | |
| 13.2d | **Podman-in-VM** for DinD (agent `run_in_terminal` with docker commands) | 2 days | Guest kernel supports cgroups natively — no privilege escalation |
| 13.2e | **Port forwarding** via reverse WS tunnel (`/proc/net/tcp` scanning in guest) | 3 days | Designed in §7.3, listed as "Planned Q1 2026" |
| 13.2f | **PID-reuse protection**: replace raw `libc::kill()` with `pidfd_open` | 1 day | Already tracked in §1.3 |
| 13.2g | **Single-binary OCI image pull + unpack**: replace the `skopeo` + `umoci` subprocess path with native image resolution, digest verification, layer unpack, whiteout handling, and rootfs caching inside `g5d` | 4 days | Goal: ship one worker binary with libkrun + image mechanics built in; no external image-tool dependencies on the worker host/image. |
| 13.2h | **Prod-grade nested-container validation**: prove a prod worker can execute `just ci-docker` for the g5 repo successfully inside the microVM using the default guest image | 2 days | This is the acceptance target for "complex Docker-in-Docker works", not just a toy `podman run hello-world`. |

**Exit criteria for 13.2 + 13.6**:

- The committed workspace config is the durable source of truth for the guest image, with a canonical `isolation.image` field (and `base_image` accepted only as a backward-compat alias).
- `g5d` can boot a configured OCI guest image without shelling out to `skopeo` or `umoci`.
- The default public guest image includes the common runtimes/mechanics needed for G5's own complex workflows, including nested-container support.
- A prod-style worker (`kata` pod, `G5D_ISOLATION_MODE=microvm`) can run `just ci-docker` in the g5 repo successfully inside the microVM.

### 13.3 GKE Deployment (Kata pods — separate concern from same-host VMs)

**Note**: Kata pods on GKE are the **production multi-tenant boundary** (one pod per worker host), NOT the per-task isolation mechanism. Each Kata pod runs one g5d process that internally boots N krunvm microVMs for N concurrent tasks. Kata gives tenant-to-tenant isolation; krunvm gives task-to-task isolation within a tenant.

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.3a | K8s manifests with `runtimeClassName: kata`, Workload Identity, network policies | 3 days | Design in WORKER_INFRASTRUCTURE.md §1; no manifests in `infra/` |
| 13.3b | Helm chart for worker pool (autoscaler, resource quotas) | 2 days | |

### 13.4 Concurrent Poll Loop (orchestration layer)

**Problem**: Even with isolation and COW ready, the poll loop itself is sequential. Making a single worker process handle N tasks concurrently requires structural changes.

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.4a | Change `current_task_id: Option<String>` → `active_tasks: Arc<DashMap<String, JoinHandle>>` | 1 day | Track N running tasks with their tokio handles |
| 13.4b | Replace sequential poll loop with semaphore-bounded `tokio::spawn` per task | 2 days | `Semaphore::new(max_concurrent_tasks)`, spawn task execution into background |
| 13.4c | `WorkerState` enum → active task count (idle when 0, executing when > 0) | 1 day | Heartbeat reports `active_task_ids: Vec<String>` (already exists) |
| 13.4d | Make `max_concurrent_tasks` configurable via `semlift.yaml` / env var | 0.5 day | Currently hardcoded to `1` |
| 13.4e | Cancel signal fan-out: per-task `CancellationToken` instead of single `watch::channel` | 1 day | Current `task_cancel_tx` is a single bool — can't cancel one task without affecting others |
| 13.4f | Heartbeat: report all `active_task_ids`, receive per-task cancellation signals | 1 day | Current heartbeat already sends `active_task_ids` |

### 13.5 Ontology COW Snapshots (DB layer — separate concern)

**Problem**: Workspace clone does full deep copy of `ontology_nodes`, `node_dependencies`, `docs`, `doc_node_links` — O(N rows). At scale (100K+ nodes), this takes 20+ seconds.

**Full design in `ONTOLOGY_COW.md`** (Option A recommended):
- `ontology_snapshots` + `ontology_snapshot_nodes` tables (immutable base layer)
- `ontology_overlay` table (per-branch COW modifications: add/modify/delete)  
- Clone becomes `UPDATE workspace_branches SET base_snapshot_id = ...` — O(1)
- Compaction when overlay > 50% of base

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.5a | Schema migration: snapshot + overlay tables | 1 day | SQL in ONTOLOGY_COW.md |
| 13.5b | Snapshot creation on commit | 2 days | Replaces deep copy in clone path |
| 13.5c | Read path: `ontology_nodes_effective` view with overlay merge | 1 day | |
| 13.5d | Compaction job | 1 day | Background cron or on-demand |

**Priority**: LOW — current deep copy works for <10K nodes. Unrelated to task concurrency.

### 13.6 Workspace-Level Image Configuration (workspace config + API gap)

**Problem**: The base OCI image for microVMs is resolved entirely on the worker side via a static chain: hardcoded default (`"g5/worker:base"`) → env var (`G5D_ISOLATION_BASE_IMAGE`) → CLI flag (`--base-image`). There is no committed workspace-config source of truth for "this workspace uses image X", and there is no API-side or DB-side concept of surfacing that choice to the shared worker pool.

This means a shared worker pool cannot serve heterogeneous workspaces (e.g., one needing Python 3.12 + CUDA, another needing Go 1.22 + protoc). Every worker on the pool uses the same image.

**What's missing**:

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.6a | Rename workspace config field to canonical `isolation.image` and keep `base_image` as a deprecated alias | 0.5 day | The committed workspace config should be the durable source of truth for guest-image selection. |
| 13.6b | Add `worker_image` column to `workspaces` table (nullable, default NULL = use pool default) | 0.5 day | Migration + model update |
| 13.6c | Include `worker_image: Option<String>` in `TaskAssignment` DTO (populated at poll time from workspace settings) | 0.5 day | `g5-common/src/types/task_assignment.rs` + `task_service.rs` poll query |
| 13.6d | `build_and_execute_task()` uses `assignment.worker_image` when present, falls back to the resolved workspace/default image | 0.5 day | In `g5d/src/worker/mod.rs`; this must stop bypassing workspace-config image selection. |
| 13.6e | UI: workspace settings panel for selecting/overriding worker image | 1 day | Frontend + API route |
| 13.6f | Image allowlist/validation: prevent arbitrary images in multi-tenant environments | 1 day | Org-level `allowed_worker_images` setting |

**Priority**: MEDIUM — not needed while all workspaces use the same toolchain stack, but blocks multi-language/multi-framework worker pools.

### 13.7 macOS MicroVM Limitations (Linux guests only)

**Problem**: `krunvm`/`libkrun` on macOS ARM64 boots a **Linux guest kernel** inside the HVF hypervisor. The OCI image (`g5/worker:base`) is a Linux container. macOS guests are not supported — Apple does not license macOS for use in third-party lightweight hypervisors like libkrun.

**Implications**:

| Scenario | What happens | Impact |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| macOS dev, language-agnostic tasks (Python, Rust, JS) | MicroVM works — Linux guest runs the same toolchains | None |
| macOS dev, macOS-specific tasks (Xcode, Swift, `xcrun`, `.framework` linking) | MicroVM guest cannot run macOS tools | Current implementation can fall back to `ProcessBackend`, but this should become an explicit operator choice or a hard error |
| macOS dev, Docker-based tasks | Podman inside Linux guest works | None |
| Intel Mac | HVF unsupported by libkrun; `check_hvf()` returns false | Current implementation falls back to `ProcessBackend`; desired behavior is fail-closed unless `process` was requested explicitly |

**Current behavior**: The `IsolationConfig.fallback` mechanism still allows
the runtime to substitute `process` when `MicroVm` is unavailable. That is now
considered debt, not the desired contract: the configured isolation mode should
be authoritative, and unsupported backends should fail closed instead of
quietly degrading to worktree-based process execution.

**Guardrail note**: `ProcessBackend` currently changes `cwd` and appends env
vars, but it does not clear inherited environment state or enforce a filesystem
boundary. If `process` remains a supported explicit mode, it needs OS-enforced
confinement or equivalent hard guardrails; path validation plus `current_dir()`
alone is not isolation.

**Why libkrun can't do macOS guests**: It uses Hypervisor.framework at the low level to boot a Linux kernel — it has no macOS boot support (no Mach-O loader, no iBoot emulation, no macOS kernel boot protocol).

**Alternatives for macOS-native isolation**:

| Technology | macOS guests? | Linux guests? | How it works | Fit for g5d |
|------------|:---:|:---:|---|---|
| **Apple Virtualization.framework** (macOS 13+) | ✅ | ✅ | Apple's first-party hypervisor API. Boots macOS from IPSW restore images. | Could wrap as a `VzBackend` — same pattern as `KrunvmBackend`. Apple allows macOS VMs on Apple hardware (EULA §2.B.iii). |
| **Tart** (open source, Apache 2.0) | ✅ | ✅ | CLI tool built on Virtualization.framework. `tart run`/`tart exec` for macOS + Linux VMs. OCI image distribution (`tart push/pull`). | Best near-term option — CLI follows same spawn pattern as krunvm. OCI images fit existing pipeline. |
| **krunkit** | ❌ | ✅ | macOS companion to libkrun, uses Virtualization.framework. Lighter than Tart but Linux guests only. | No advantage over current krunvm for macOS-native work. |
| **`sandbox-exec` + SBPL profiles** | N/A (not a VM) | N/A | macOS BSD-level sandbox. Restricts file access, network, IPC per process. No separate kernel. Deprecated API but still functional. | Lightweight alternative: g5d calls `sandbox-exec -f profile.sb -- <agent-cmd>` to restrict tool execution to worktree + control plane endpoints. Weaker than VM but zero boot overhead. |
| **`sandbox_init()` C API** | N/A | N/A | Programmatic version of sandbox-exec. Apply sandbox before `exec()`. | Could be called in `ProcessBackend::run()` on macOS before spawning the child process. |

**Recommended approach** (tiered):

1. **Linux-compatible workloads on Mac** (most cases): Current `KrunvmBackend` via HVF — already works.
2. **macOS-native workloads** (Xcode, Swift, xcrun): Add a `TartBackend` implementing `MicrovmBackend` trait. Tart's CLI (`tart clone`, `tart run`, `tart exec`) maps cleanly to `start()`/`run()`/`kill()`. OCI distribution means the same image pipeline. macOS IPSW base images via `tart create --from-ipsw`.
3. **Lightweight sandboxing** (when VM overhead is too much): Add a `SandboxBackend` for macOS using `sandbox-exec` + a custom SBPL profile restricting the agent to the worktree directory, blocking network except control plane + GCS endpoints.

**What's missing**:

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 13.7a | `TartBackend` implementing `MicrovmBackend` trait — `start()` via `tart clone` + `tart run`, `run()` via `tart exec`, `kill()` via `tart stop` | 3 days | Mirrors `KrunvmBackend` structure. Detect via `find_binary("tart")` in `detect.rs`. |
| 13.7b | macOS base VM image pipeline: IPSW-based macOS image with Xcode CLI tools, pushed to OCI registry via `tart push` | 2 days | Image is large (~20 GB); needs local caching strategy. |
| 13.7c | `SandboxBackend` for lightweight macOS sandboxing — generate SBPL profile restricting file access to worktree + cache dirs, network to control plane + GCS | 2 days | Implements `MicrovmBackend` with `IsolationLevel::Container` (between Process and Vm). Use as an explicitly selected backend, not as a silent fallback. |
| 13.7d | `BackendType::Tart` + `BackendType::Sandbox` variants in enum and detection pipeline | 1 day | Add to `detect_backends()` and validate configured backend availability. Backend selection should honor configured mode and error if unavailable. |
| 13.7e | Workspace-level `requires_native_host: bool` flag — task assignment skips Linux-guest workers and routes to Tart/Process workers on matching OS | 1 day | Needs `worker_os`/`worker_arch` in worker registration + `TaskAssignment` routing filter |
| 13.7f | Worker registration: report `host_os` and `host_arch` alongside capabilities | 0.5 day | Currently not reported; `poll_for_task` has no OS affinity filter |
| 13.7g | Documentation: clarify in `semlift.yaml` that `mode: microvm` = Linux guest, `mode: tart` = macOS guest | 0.5 day | |

**Priority**: LOW-MEDIUM — most G5 workloads are language-agnostic. Matters for iOS/macOS-native development workflows (Xcode, SwiftUI, xctest). `SandboxBackend` (13.7c) is independently useful as a zero-overhead sandboxing layer for desktop workers on macOS.

### Summary & Prioritization

The critical path to concurrent tasks is: **COW overlay (13.1a) → concurrent poll loop (13.4a–f) → done**. Everything else is independent.

| Phase | Items | Est. Total | Priority | Dependency |
|-------|-------|-----------|----------|------------|
| **A** COW + concurrent loop | 13.1a/b, 13.4a–f | ~9 days | **HIGH** | None — this IS the concurrency unlock |
| **B** GCS repo snapshots (cloud cold start) | 13.1c, 13.1d | ~3 days | **MEDIUM** | GCS bucket + IAM |
| **C** Guest image + single-binary OCI + DinD + port fwd | 13.2b–h | ~14 days | **MEDIUM** | Phase A |
| **D** GKE Kata deployment | 13.3a–b | ~5 days | **HIGH (prod)** | GKE cluster with Kata runtime class |
| **E** Ontology COW | 13.5a–d | ~5 days | **LOW** | None |
| **F** Workspace image config | 13.6a–f | ~4.5 days | **MEDIUM** | Phase C (default guest image + in-binary OCI path should exist first) |
| **G** macOS native isolation | 13.7a–d | ~8 days | **LOW-MEDIUM** | None (Tart is independent of krunvm pipeline) |
| **H** OS affinity routing | 13.7e–g | ~2 days | **LOW** | Phase F + G |

## 14. Git Mirror Mode — g5-api as Repo Storage Backend

**Priority**: MEDIUM — enables private repo workflows without granting g5 direct SCM access.

### Problem

Currently g5-api only acquires repo content via `repo_fetcher`, which does `git clone`/`git fetch` from the remote URL. This requires the server to have read access to the repo. For private repos where the user cannot (or will not) grant g5 SCM credentials, there is no way to get code into the system.

The `g5d add` CLI clones repos locally using the user's own credentials, but there is no mechanism to upload that content to g5-api's storage. The worker therefore has no code to analyze when an uplift job runs.

### Proposed Solution

Allow g5-api to act as a **git mirror** — users push repo content directly to g5-api rather than relying on g5-api to pull from the remote.

| # | Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 14.1 | `POST /api/v1/repos/:id/bundle` endpoint — accepts a git bundle upload, unbundles into `/data/repos/<repo_id>` bare repo | 2 days | Multipart upload, size limits, streaming to disk. Must validate bundle integrity before replacing existing repo. |
| 14.2 | `g5d add --mirror` flag — after cloning locally, creates a `git bundle` and uploads it to g5-api via the bundle endpoint | 1 day | Uses `git bundle create --all` to capture all refs. Falls back to error if API unreachable. |
| 14.3 | `g5d push --mirror` variant — re-bundles and uploads incremental changes to g5-api | 1 day | Incremental bundles (`git bundle create --since` or basis negotiation). Updates `workspace.lock` after successful upload. |
| 14.4 | `repo_fetcher` skip logic — skip fetch for repos that have no remote URL or are marked as mirror-only | 0.5 day | Add `mirror_mode: bool` column to `repos` table, or infer from NULL `git_url`. |
| 14.5 | Frontend "Upload repo" option in AddRepoDialog — alternative to "paste URL" for private repos | 1 day | Drag-and-drop `.bundle` file or trigger `g5d add --mirror` from IDE plugin. |

**Total estimate**: ~5.5 days

### User Flow

```
# User clones private repo locally with their credentials
g5d add git@github.com:corp/private-repo.git --mirror

# g5d clones locally, bundles, uploads to g5-api
# → g5-api unbundles into /data/repos/<id>
# → uplift job is auto-created (existing add_repo behavior)
# → worker picks up bootstrap, analyzes code

# Later, to sync updates:
g5d push --mirror
```

### Dependencies

None — independent of worker concurrency (§13) and SCM integration.

## 15. Repo Management — Error Handling & Removal

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Dev-stack tinydb uplift — bootstrap completed with 0 tasks because the repo's `default_branch` was stored as `main` but the actual remote uses `master`. The indexer clone failed silently and the worker timed out waiting for it.

### §15.1 — Default branch auto-detection on add-repo

**Problem**: When a repo is added to a workspace, the API stores `default_branch = "main"` without querying the remote. Repos that use `master`, `develop`, or other conventions fail silently — the indexer clone succeeds but can't resolve `refs/remotes/origin/main`, the worker times out, and the bootstrap completes as a no-op with zero tasks.

**Fix**: On `add_repo`, run `git ls-remote --symref <url> HEAD` to detect the actual default branch before inserting. Fall back to `main` only if detection fails, and surface a warning.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

### §15.2 — Clear error surfacing for failed repo clones

**Problem**: When the indexer fails to clone or fetch a repo the error is logged but not surfaced to the user. The bootstrap task completes successfully (status=completed) even though the target repo was never analyzed. The UI shows no indication that anything went wrong.

**Fix**: 
- Add a `clone_status` (or `sync_status`) column to `repos` — values: `pending`, `cloned`, `failed`.
- Indexer `repo_fetcher` should update this status on success/failure.
- Bootstrap should check repo clone status before proceeding; if the target repo isn't cloned, fail the bootstrap task with a descriptive error rather than silently completing.
- Frontend should display repo sync status in the workspace settings / repo list.

**Estimate**: 1 day

### §15.3 — Remove repo from workspace

**Problem**: There is no API endpoint or UI flow to remove a repo from a workspace. If a repo is added with the wrong URL or is no longer needed, the only recourse is manual database surgery.

**Fix**:
- Add `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:ws_id/repos/:repo_id` endpoint with `workspaces:admin` scope.
- Cascade-delete the `workspace_branches` entries, associated ontology nodes, and tasks.
- Clean up the on-disk clone in `/data/repos/<repo_id>`.
- Add a "Remove repo" action in the frontend workspace settings panel.

**Estimate**: 1.5 days

### Summary

| # | Item | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|
| 15.1 | Auto-detect default branch on add-repo | 0.5 day |
| 15.2 | Surface clone/fetch failures to user | 1 day |
| 15.3 | Remove repo from workspace | 1.5 days |

**Total estimate**: 3 days
## 16. Project Switcher — Non-Functional Workspace Switching & Creation

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Manual QA review of the TopBar project switcher dropdown.

The `WorkspaceSwitcher` component in the TopBar renders a fully functional-looking dropdown (search, workspace list, "New Project" button) but **does nothing** when a user selects a workspace or clicks "New Project". The underlying callbacks are wired to no-ops in the only production consumer.

### §16.1 — `onSelectWorkspace` is a no-op on WorkspacePage

**Problem**: [WorkspacePage.tsx](generation/client/src/pages/WorkspacePage.tsx#L2250) passes `onSelectWorkspace={() => {}}` to `TopBar`, which forwards it to `WorkspaceSwitcher`. Users can open the dropdown, search workspaces, and click one — nothing happens. The dropdown closes but no navigation occurs.

**Root cause**: The `ProjectsPage` has a working implementation of `handleSelectWorkspace` that resolves the workspace name and navigates via `navigate(\`/\${orgSlug}/\${ws.name}\`)`. This same pattern was never replicated in `WorkspacePage`. The `WorkspacePage` component has `useNavigate()` and `useParams()` available (line 1197), so the fix is straightforward.

**Fix**:
```tsx
// In WorkspacePage, replace:
onSelectWorkspace={() => {}}
// With:
onSelectWorkspace={(id) => {
  // Resolve workspace name from the workspace list and navigate
  // Requires access to org slug + workspace name lookup
  navigate(`/${org}/${workspaceName}`);
}}
```

This requires either:
1. Passing the workspaces list (from `useWorkspaces`) into scope so the selected ID can be resolved to a name/slug for the URL, **or**
2. Changing the route scheme to accept workspace IDs directly (breaking change), **or**
3. Having `WorkspaceSwitcher` pass both `id` and `name` in its callback signature.

Option (1) is the simplest: call `useWorkspaces(resolvedOrgId)` in `WorkspacePage` and look up the selected workspace's name for navigation. The `ProjectsPage` already does this pattern successfully.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

### §16.2 — `onNewWorkspace` is a no-op on WorkspacePage

**Problem**: [TopBar.tsx](generation/client/src/components/workspace/TopBar.tsx#L399-L401) passes `onNewWorkspace={() => { /* handled by WorkspaceSwitcher internally */ }}` — but `WorkspaceSwitcher` does **not** handle it internally. It calls `onNewWorkspace()` on click and closes the dropdown. The comment is misleading.

The `ProjectsPage` has a working implementation: it renders `CreateWorkspaceDialog` conditionally and sets `createDialogOpen` state to `true` when "New Project" is clicked. `WorkspacePage` has no equivalent state or dialog.

**Fix**: Add `createDialogOpen` state to `WorkspacePage`, render `CreateWorkspaceDialog` when open, and wire `onNewWorkspace` to set it. After creation, navigate to the new workspace. The `ProjectsPage` implementation at [ProjectsPage.tsx](generation/client/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx#L125-L145) can be used as a reference.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

### §16.3 — `useCreateWorkspace` unused import in `WorkspaceSwitcher`

**Problem**: [WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx](generation/client/src/components/workspace/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx#L15) imports `useCreateWorkspace` but never uses it. This suggests an incomplete implementation where workspace creation was intended to be handled inside the switcher but was never wired up.

**Fix**: Either remove the unused import (if creation stays in a dialog) or implement inline creation. The current architecture delegates creation to `CreateWorkspaceDialog`, so removing the import is correct.

**Estimate**: 5 min

### §16.4 — Workspace list not fetched on WorkspacePage for switcher

**Problem**: The `WorkspaceSwitcher` calls `useWorkspaces(orgId)` to populate its dropdown. This works, but the `orgId` prop comes from `TopBar`, which receives it from `WorkspacePage` as `resolvedOrgId || org || ''`. If `resolvedOrgId` hasn't loaded yet (the `useResolveWorkspaceSlug` hook is async), the orgId may briefly be the raw URL slug rather than a UUID, which could cause the workspaces query to fail or return empty results.

**Fix**: Ensure the `WorkspaceSwitcher` receives the resolved org UUID, not the URL slug. Guard the workspaces query with `enabled: !!orgId && isUuid(orgId)` or wait for slug resolution.

**Estimate**: 0.25 day

### §16.5 — No `/projects` route accessible from workspace view

**Problem**: There is no UI element in the `WorkspacePage` (TopBar, sidebar, etc.) that links back to the `/projects` listing page. A user inside a workspace has no way to navigate to the full project list except by manually editing the URL. The `WorkspaceSwitcher` dropdown is the only navigation aid, and it's broken (§16.1).

**Fix**: Add a link/button in the TopBar or left sidebar that navigates to `/projects`. Alternatively, ensure the G5 logo/branding in TopBar links to `/projects` or `/`.

**Estimate**: 0.25 day

### Summary

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 16.1 | `onSelectWorkspace` no-op on WorkspacePage | **HIGH** — core navigation broken | 0.5 day |
| 16.2 | `onNewWorkspace` no-op on WorkspacePage | **HIGH** — cannot create project from workspace | 0.5 day |
| 16.3 | Unused `useCreateWorkspace` import | LOW — dead code | 5 min |
| 16.4 | Org ID may be slug instead of UUID for switcher query | MEDIUM — intermittent empty dropdown | 0.25 day |
| 16.5 | No route back to `/projects` from workspace | MEDIUM — navigation dead end | 0.25 day |

**Total estimate**: 1.5 days

## 17. Ontology Branch Isolation — Nodes Updated Immediately Instead of on Merge

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Manual QA of uplift job flow — ontology tree updates in the UI as soon as bootstrap runs, even before the user clicks "Merge". Cancelling a job leaves the ontology in a dirty state.

### Problem

The ontology tree is workspace-level metadata with no branch isolation. When a job's bootstrap task runs waterfall analysis, it calls `POST /api/internal/workspaces/:id/ontology/upsert` ([bootstrap.rs line 259](generation/g5d/src/worker/bootstrap.rs#L259)), which writes nodes **directly** to the `ontology_nodes` table against the first `workspace_branch` it finds ([internal.rs line 1134](generation/g5-api/src/routes/internal.rs#L1134): `SELECT id FROM workspace_branches WHERE workspace_id = $1 LIMIT 1`).

The frontend reads the same table via `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:id/ontology` → `ontology_service.get_ontology_tree()` which joins `ontology_nodes` on `workspace_branches` for the workspace.

This means:
1. **Ontology appears immediately** — before the user decides to merge or cancel.
2. **Cancelling a job doesn't revert ontology** — `rollback_job` only reverts git branches, not ontology rows.
3. **Concurrent jobs clobber each other** — if `preserve_existing_hierarchy = false`, the upsert deletes all existing nodes first.
4. **No diff/preview** — the user can't see "what ontology changes will this job produce" before committing.

The merge/cancel buttons only control **git branch merges** (fast-forward of job branch into base branch). The ontology is decoupled from this flow entirely.

### Proposed Fix

Introduce a `job_id` column on `ontology_nodes` to track which job produced each node, and a `committed` boolean (or `status` enum) to gate visibility.

#### §17.1 — Add `job_id` + `committed` columns to `ontology_nodes`

Add a migration:
```sql
ALTER TABLE ontology_nodes
  ADD COLUMN job_id UUID REFERENCES jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  ADD COLUMN committed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true;

-- Existing nodes are already committed (pre-existing data).
```

New nodes inserted by the upsert endpoint get `job_id = <current_job>` and `committed = false`.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

#### §17.2 — Filter uncommitted nodes from the read path

Update `ontology_service.get_ontology_tree()` to add `WHERE n.committed = true` (or `n.job_id IS NULL OR n.committed = true`) so uncommitted nodes are invisible until merge.

Optionally expose a `?include_uncommitted=true` query parameter for the task detail view, so users can preview what a running job will produce.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

#### §17.3 — Commit ontology on merge

In `workspace_service::merge_workspace()`, after successfully merging git branches, set `committed = true` for all nodes belonging to jobs associated with that workspace:

```sql
UPDATE ontology_nodes
SET committed = true
WHERE job_id IN (
  SELECT id FROM jobs
  WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND status = 'completed'
) AND committed = false;
```

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

#### §17.4 — Revert ontology on cancel/rollback

In `job_service::rollback_job()`, delete uncommitted nodes for the rolled-back job:

```sql
DELETE FROM ontology_nodes
WHERE job_id = $1 AND committed = false;
```

This cleanly removes the proposed ontology changes without affecting previously committed nodes.

**Estimate**: 0.25 day

#### §17.5 — Pass `job_id` through the upsert endpoint

Update the `upsert_ontology_nodes` internal endpoint and the worker's `UpsertOntologyNodesRequest` to include an optional `job_id`. The worker already knows its job ID in the bootstrap context. The endpoint sets `committed = false` and `job_id = <value>` on all inserted/updated rows.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

#### §17.6 — Frontend: show pending ontology with visual distinction

When `include_uncommitted=true` is used, render uncommitted nodes with a visual indicator (e.g., dashed border, "pending" badge, or reduced opacity) so users can distinguish proposed changes from committed structure. This is optional for MVP.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day (optional)

### Alternative Approach: Shadow Table

Instead of adding columns, use a separate `ontology_nodes_draft` table with an identical schema plus `job_id`. Bootstrap writes to the draft table; merge copies to `ontology_nodes`; rollback deletes from draft. This avoids schema changes to the production table but adds duplication.

The `committed` column approach is simpler and preferred.

### Summary

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 17.1 | Add `job_id` + `committed` columns | **HIGH** — schema change, migration | 0.5 day |
| 17.2 | Filter uncommitted from read path | **HIGH** — prevents premature display | 0.5 day |
| 17.3 | Commit ontology on merge | **HIGH** — completes the isolation | 0.5 day |
| 17.4 | Revert ontology on cancel/rollback | **HIGH** — cleanup on discard | 0.25 day |
| 17.5 | Pass `job_id` through upsert endpoint | **HIGH** — plumbing for isolation | 0.5 day |
| 17.6 | Frontend pending node visuals | MEDIUM — UX polish, optional | 0.5 day |

**Total estimate**: 2.75 days (2.25 days without §17.6)

## 18. Spec Storage Location — Specs Written to Source Repo Instead of Docs Repo

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Live dev uplift of TinyDB — all `.semlift/specs/` files are committed to the source repo (tinydb) rather than the docs repo.

### Problem

The design ([DESIGN.md §2.1–§2.4](generation/designs/DESIGN.md#L87)) specifies that:
- **Specs** are per-repo design artifacts stored at `.g5/specs/` (or `.semlift/specs/`) inside each repo, committed to the repo's git history.
- **Docs** live in a dedicated workspace-level docs repo (`.g5/docs/`), separate from source repos.

Currently, `workspace_git_url` in task assignments is resolved by `task_service.rs` with an ORDER BY that **deprioritizes** the docs repo (rank 3), so all tasks execute against the source repo. This means:

1. **All specs land in the source repo** — both source-derived specs (`tinydb/utils.semlift.md`) and docs-derived specs (`docs/_themes/flask_theme_support.semlift.md`) end up in `.semlift/specs/` under the tinydb repo checkout.
2. **Docs repo is empty** — the docs repo (`ad7f8b64`) at `/data/repos/ad7f8b64-.../` has zero spec files.
3. **Downlift bootstrap uses `repos[0]`** — if `repos[0]` happens to be the docs repo (non-deterministic SQL ordering), spec reads fail and tasks lose inter-dependency information.
4. **No workspace-level `.g5/` umbrella** — the server layout is flat (`/data/repos/{uuid}/`), not the hierarchical `<workspace>/.g5/docs/` + `<workspace>/repos/` structure from the design.

### Current Behavior (Acceptable for Now)

Storing all specs in the source repo works correctly for single-source-repo workspaces. The waterfall analyzer already namespaces specs by project name (e.g., `tinydb/utils`, `docs/_themes/flask_theme_support`), so there are no collisions. Workers read/write specs and commit to a single repo — simple and functional.

### Future Considerations

For multi-source-repo workspaces (e.g., a workspace with `backend/`, `frontend/`, and `shared-types/`), the current approach breaks down:

- **Which source repo gets the specs?** The ORDER BY picks one, but specs for other repos would be orphaned in the wrong repo.
- **Cross-repo specs** (workspace-level design docs) have no natural home in any single source repo.
- **Merge flows** become complex — merging a job branch means merging into multiple repos, but specs only live in one.

#### Option A: Specs in Source Repos (per-repo isolation)
Each repo gets its own `.semlift/specs/` containing only specs for files in that repo. Requires routing spec writes to the correct repo based on `component_id → repo` mapping.

#### Option B: Specs in Docs Repo (centralized)
All specs go into the docs repo. Requires adding `docs_repo_path` to `TaskAssignment`, routing spec read/write to the docs repo, and committing to the docs repo (alongside or instead of the source repo).

#### Option C: Workspace Umbrella Directory
Create a workspace-level directory on disk matching the design:
```
/data/workspaces/{workspace_id}/
├── .g5/
│   ├── workspace-meta/
│   └── docs/  → /data/repos/{docs_repo_id}
├── repos/
│   ├── backend/ → /data/repos/{backend_repo_id}
│   └── frontend/ → /data/repos/{frontend_repo_id}
```
Symlinks or bind mounts map repo UUIDs to human-readable paths. Workers operate on the workspace root.

### Decision

Deferred. Current single-source-repo behavior is acceptable for MVP. Revisit when multi-source-repo workspaces are prioritized.

### Migration Track — Centralize The Active Ontology In The Docs Repo

If we explicitly choose the docs repo as the canonical home for the active
workspace ontology, that is a product-direction change rather than something
the current runtime already supports.

Today:

- bootstrap/downlift discovers one specs root by searching repo checkouts for
  `.semlift/specs` or `.g5/specs`
- spec tooling reads and writes specs relative to that checkout root
- docs are materialized separately under `.g5/docs`

That means moving the ontology into the docs repo requires an intentional
migration plan:

1. add a first-class docs-repo ontology path to task assignment / worker inputs
2. route spec read/write, bootstrap, and downlift through that docs checkout
3. define how source-file-relative specs map back to multiple source repos
4. update clone/refresh/commit/push so ontology versioning is docs-repo-native
5. migrate existing repo-local spec trees without breaking component identity

This should be tracked explicitly if we decide the long-term operator
experience is "clone one docs repo to get the whole ontology" rather than
"each repo owns its slice of the ontology."

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 18.1 | Route spec writes to correct repo (Option A) | MEDIUM | 1.5 days |

## 19. Newly Created Docs in Views Are Not Editable in Rich Mode

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Manual testing — creating a document via CreateDocDialog, then clicking it in the Views sidebar section.

### Problem

When a user creates a new document (via the "+" button in Project Docs) and the doc has no `#!internal-workspace-` prefix in its path (which is the default), it appears in the **Views** sidebar section. Clicking on it opens the SpecEditor in rich mode with `editable={true}`, but the editor is completely empty with no way to start typing.

**Root cause**: Three issues combine to produce this bug:

1. **Backend returns `content: null` for new docs** — `doc_service.rs` `get_doc()` reads content from git via `file_path + docs_repo_id`. A newly created doc typically has no `file_path` or no file on disk yet, so `content` is `None` (serialized as `null`).

2. **Frontend coerces null content to empty string** — In `WorkspacePage.tsx` `ContentDispatch`, the doc content branch does:
   ```tsx
   const docContentStr = docContent.data.content ?? '';
   ```
   This passes `''` as the `content` prop to `SpecEditor`.

3. **`parseMarkdownToBlocks('')` returns `[]`** — In `utils.ts`, `parseMarkdownToBlocks` starts with `if (!markdown) return []`. Empty string is falsy, so zero blocks are produced. The rich-mode grid (`blocks.map(...)`) renders nothing — no `SpecBlock`, no `EditableInline`, no place for the user to click or type.

**Source mode works** — switching to source mode shows a `<textarea>` that accepts input. But the default rich mode is broken for empty docs.

### Affected Files

| File | Line(s) | Issue |
|------|---------|-------|
| [client/src/lib/utils.ts](generation/client/src/lib/utils.ts#L820) | 820 | `parseMarkdownToBlocks` returns `[]` for empty/falsy input |
| [client/src/components/editor/SpecEditor.tsx](generation/client/src/components/editor/SpecEditor.tsx#L2371) | 2371 | `blocks.map(...)` renders nothing when blocks is empty |
| [client/src/pages/WorkspacePage.tsx](generation/client/src/pages/WorkspacePage.tsx#L1098) | 1098 | `docContentStr` coerces null → '' with no placeholder |
| [g5-api/src/services/doc_service.rs](generation/g5-api/src/services/doc_service.rs#L210) | 206–235 | `get_doc` returns `content: None` when no file exists on disk |

### Fix Options

**Option A (Frontend — recommended)**: When `blocks` is empty and `editable` is true, render a single empty paragraph block as a starter. This is how Notion, Google Docs, etc. handle blank documents — show an empty editable line with a placeholder like "Start writing…".

```tsx
// In SpecEditor, after computing blocks:
const displayBlocks = blocks.length === 0 && editable
  ? [{ type: 'paragraph' as const, content: '' }]
  : blocks;
```

**Option B (Frontend + Backend)**: Have `create_doc` return a default content body (e.g. `# <doc name>\n\n`) so the doc is never truly empty. The backend seed script already does something similar for pre-populated docs.

**Option C (Frontend — minimal)**: Add an "empty state" UI in the SpecEditor that shows a clickable placeholder. On click, seed the CRDT with an initial paragraph block and switch to editing.

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 19.1 | Add empty-doc starter block in SpecEditor rich mode (Option A) | HIGH | 0.5 day |
| 19.2 | Seed default content in `create_doc` API (Option B) | MEDIUM | 0.5 day |
| 19.3 | Add placeholder empty-state UI in SpecEditor (Option C) | LOW | 0.5 day |

## 20. Worker Commit Propagation — Local-Only, Cloud Not Yet Supported

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Updated**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Implementation of CoW-based per-task workspace isolation and local git mirroring.

### What Was Implemented

A complete local-mode commit propagation pipeline that handles concurrent, isolated per-task workspaces:

1. **`fetch_local()`** on `GitRepo` ([repo.rs](generation/g5-common/src/git/repo.rs#L114)) — fetches refs from a local path via anonymous remote. No authentication needed. Used to mirror task branch objects from CoW copies back into the source repo before cleanup.

2. **`merge_branch_no_checkout()`** on `GitRepo` ([repo.rs](generation/g5-common/src/git/repo.rs#L143)) — in-memory three-way merge via `git2::merge_trees`. Creates a merge commit on the target branch without modifying the working directory or HEAD. Used to merge `task/{task_id}` into the job branch.

3. **Worker mirror + merge step** ([mod.rs](generation/g5d/src/worker/mod.rs#L1165)) — after task lifecycle completes:
   - CoW copies: `fetch_local` to bring task branch objects into source repo
   - Both CoW and worktree: `merge_branch_no_checkout(task_branch, job_branch)` so the job branch ref includes all task work

4. **CAS gate relaxed** ([task_service.rs](generation/g5-api/src/services/task_service.rs#L1138)) — concurrent isolated tasks all share the same `base_commit`, so strict CAS was changed from hard reject to warning. DB `head_commit` is now advisory.

5. **Auto-merge reads git ref** ([task_service.rs](generation/g5-api/src/services/task_service.rs#L1411)) — at job completion, `resolve_branch_head(job_branch)` reads the actual `refs/heads/{job_branch}` from git rather than relying on `jobs.head_commit` from the DB. This picks up merge commits that include all task work.

### Local Dev Flow (working)

```
  Task commits in         fetch_local           merge_branch_no_checkout
  isolated CoW copy  ────────────────▶  Source repo  ────────────────────▶  Job branch
  (task/{id} branch)    (objects back)  (task/{id}     (task/{id} merged     includes all
                                         branch now     into job/{job_id})    task work)
                              │                │                  │
                              └────────────────┴──────────────────┘
                                   Shared Docker volume mount
                                        ┌───────┐
                              Worker ◀══╪═══════╪══▶ API
                                        └───────┘
  ✓ git objects visible to API (shared volume)
  ✓ job branch ref includes all merged task work
  ✓ API auto-merge at job completion reads git ref → fast-forwards base branch
```

### Cloud/Prod Flow (not yet supported)

```
  Worker pod's /data/repos/...          API server's /data/repos/...
  (local SSD)                           (separate disk)
              ╳ no transport ╳
  ✓ commit_sha reported via REST
  ✗ git objects NOT on API server — SHA is unresolvable
  ✗ merge commits on job branch exist only on worker pod
```

### Remaining Work for Cloud

Requires a transport mechanism to move git objects from worker pods to the API server. §14 (Git Mirror Mode) proposes bundle infrastructure that could be reused:

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate | Notes |
|---|------|----------|----------|-------|
| 20.1 | Worker `git bundle` + upload after merge step | **HIGH** — required for cloud workers | 1 day | Worker creates an incremental bundle covering the job branch range, uploads via `POST /api/internal/repos/:id/bundle`. API unbundles into its local bare repo. Reuses §14 bundle endpoint. |
| 20.2 | Alternative: `git push` over SSH/HTTPS to API-hosted repo | MEDIUM | 1.5 days | Requires g5-api to expose repos via git protocol (e.g., `git-http-backend` or SSH). More complex but eliminates the bundle serialization step. Worker already has `GitRepo::push()`. |
| 20.3 | Fallback: attach spec files as task result payload | MEDIUM | 0.5 day | Include generated spec content in the REST transition payload. API writes files directly. Loses git history but works immediately as a stopgap. |

**Recommended path**: §20.1 (bundle upload) — reuses §14 infrastructure, keeps git history, single code path for user ingestion and worker propagation.

### Decision

Local mode is fully implemented and sufficient for the current single-machine deployment. Cloud transport deferred until cloud workers ship.

## 21. Repo Readiness State Machine — Bootstrap / Job Gating

*Added: 2026-03-02*

### Problem

The current system has a race between **job creation** and **repo cloning**.
When a user adds a repo and triggers an uplift in quick succession (or the
UI does both atomically), the bootstrap task may start before
`repo_fetcher` completes the initial clone.  Today the worker papers over
this with a polling backoff loop (180 s timeout), but:

1. The timeout is fragile — it must exceed `FETCH_SWEEP_INTERVAL` (120 s)
   plus the clone duration; large repos can exceed this.
2. The worker spins doing nothing for up to 3 minutes even when repos are
   ready sooner.
3. If the timeout fires, bootstrap silently proceeds without the missing
   repo(s), producing an incomplete task graph with no user-visible error.

### Desired State

An explicit **repo readiness state machine** at the API level:

```
add_repo → repo_status = 'cloning'
repo_fetcher clone done → repo_status = 'ready'
create_job → gate: all workspace repos must be 'ready'
             OR: job starts in 'waiting_repos' status
             → transitions to 'bootstrapping' once all repos are 'ready'
```

This eliminates the worker-side polling entirely and gives the UI a clear
signal to show a "cloning…" indicator per repo.

### Current Workaround

Worker waits up to 180 s with exponential backoff (1 s → 30 s cap) in
`execute_bootstrap_task()` before proceeding without missing repos.

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 21.1 | Add `clone_status` column to `workspace_repos` | LOW | 0.5 day |
| 21.2 | `repo_fetcher` updates status on clone success/failure | LOW | 0.5 day |
| 21.3 | Gate job creation on repo readiness (or add `waiting_repos` job state) | MEDIUM | 1 day |
| 21.4 | Remove worker-side polling loop once API gating is in place | LOW | 0.5 day |

**Total estimate for cloud support**: 1–2 days (§20.1 or §20.3)

## 23. Nested / Sub-Workspaces — No Parent–Child Hierarchy

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Discovered during**: Manual QA — creating a new project from within an existing workspace produces a flat, top-level workspace with no structural relationship to the workspace it was created from.

The workspace data model is currently flat. There is no concept of a workspace being a "child" or "sub-workspace" of another. Every workspace lives at the same level under an org. This limits the ability to organize large projects into scoped sub-tasks or feature branches that inherit context from a parent.

### §23.1 — `CreateWorkspaceInput` has no `parentId` field

**Problem**: The `CreateWorkspaceInput` type accepts `name`, `description`, `dependencies`, and `branches` — but no `parentId`. There is no way to express that a new workspace is a child of an existing one.

**Backend**: The `workspaces` table has `cloned_from_id` (for clone provenance) but no `parent_id` column for structural hierarchy.

**Fix**:
- Add `parent_id UUID REFERENCES workspaces(id)` column to the `workspaces` table.
- Extend `CreateWorkspaceInput` with an optional `parentId` field.
- API validation: parent must exist and belong to the same org.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day (backend schema + API)

### §23.2 — Frontend has no UI for creating sub-workspaces

**Problem**: The `CreateWorkspaceDialog` has no field or option to select a parent workspace. When triggered from the project switcher inside an existing workspace, it creates a new top-level workspace with no relationship to the current one.

**Fix**:
- When `CreateWorkspaceDialog` is opened from within a workspace, pre-populate a "Parent workspace" field with the current workspace.
- Allow clearing the parent to create a top-level workspace instead.
- Consider inheriting the parent's repos/branches as defaults.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

### §23.3 — `WorkspaceSummary` / `WorkspaceDetail` have no hierarchy fields

**Problem**: Neither the summary nor detail types include `parentId` or `children`. The workspace list, switcher, and projects page render a flat list with no visual hierarchy.

**Fix**:
- Add `parentId: string | null` and optionally `childCount: number` to `WorkspaceSummary`.
- Add `children: WorkspaceSummary[]` to `WorkspaceDetail`.
- Update the projects page and workspace switcher to render nested workspaces as an indented tree or grouped list.

**Estimate**: 1 day

### §23.4 — Workspace `dependencies` vs. parent–child relationship

**Problem**: `CreateWorkspaceInput.dependencies` allows declaring cross-workspace ontology edges, but this is a DAG of independent peers, not structural nesting. The distinction between "depends on" (peer) and "is a sub-task of" (parent–child) needs to be clear in both the data model and UI.

**Fix**: Document the semantics. `dependencies` = peer DAG edges for cross-workspace ontology references. `parentId` = structural containment (sub-workspace inherits parent context, shows in tree).

**Estimate**: 0.25 day (documentation + type comments)

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 23.1 | `parentId` column + API field | HIGH — no backend support | 0.5 day |
| 23.2 | Sub-workspace creation UI | MEDIUM — no way to create nested | 0.5 day |

| 23.4 | Document dependencies vs. parent–child semantics | LOW — conceptual clarity | 0.25 day |

**Total estimate**: ~2.25 days

## 24. Separation of Concerns — Git Write Path in g5-api

**Date added**: 2026-03-02  
**Updated**: 2026-03-02 (refined boundary after architecture discussion)  
**Discovered during**: Architecture review of g5d / g5-api / g5-common boundaries.

### Intended architecture

- **G5D** — agent, task execution, workspace ↔ git integration (the "worker")
- **G5-API** — workspace hosting, CRDT authority, commit-on-flush, local indexer (ontology reconciliation), doc-friendly interfaces for non-engineer users, control plane
- **G5-UI** — UI over operations

### Refined boundary: g5-api as CRDT authority + indexer + doc interface

After discussion, the cleanest separation is:

**g5-api owns four coupled responsibilities:**
1. **CRDT authority** — Yjs WebSocket host, snapshot persistence, awareness
2. **Workspace commit on CRDT flush** — when the CRDT document flushes/compacts, g5-api atomically materializes the document and produces a git commit
3. **Local indexer** — ontology reconciliation ([ontology_reconciler.rs](generation/g5-api/src/maintenance/ontology_reconciler.rs)) on the local repo state, maintaining the ontology graph that powers doc-friendly interfaces
4. **SCM credential management & provider logic** — OAuth flows for connecting GitHub/GitLab/Google accounts ([auth/oauth.rs](generation/g5-api/src/auth/oauth.rs)), AES-256-GCM token encryption/decryption at rest ([auth/scm.rs](generation/g5-api/src/auth/scm.rs) → `ScmTokenManager`), token refresh for expiring providers (GitLab 2-hour tokens), authenticated clone URL construction (`build_clone_url`), and repo listing from provider APIs ([auth_service.rs](generation/g5-api/src/services/auth_service.rs) `ScmRepoListResponse`). g5-api is the **credential authority** — g5d never stores or manages tokens. When g5-api dispatches a `repo_sync` task (§24.6), it includes a short-lived authenticated URL so g5d can perform the git network I/O without holding credentials.

Remote repo operations (clone, fetch, rebase, push) are **g5d responsibilities** — see §24.6 for how g5-api triggers refreshes. g5d receives credential-bearing URLs from g5-api per-task and never persists them.

These are coherent because they form a **read-write loop for document-oriented users**: the local indexer ingests repo state → builds the ontology → users edit specs/docs via CRDT → edits flush to git commits → the indexer picks up changes. The remote repo is simply an external connection that g5d syncs via rebase. g5-api is the sole credential authority and never exposes raw tokens — it constructs authenticated URLs on-demand and passes them to g5d in task payloads.

**g5d owns all task execution, remote repo sync, and discretionary git operations:**
- Remote repo operations: clone, fetch, rebase, push to origin
- Job branch creation (prepare phase of first task)
- Job completion/rollback merges (post-completion lifecycle step)
- Workspace merges (internal task)
- All agent loops, LLM calls, tool execution, code generation

### What's already clean

- **g5d → g5-api**: g5d depends on `g5-common` with only the `http-client` feature flag. `sqlx` is explicitly excluded ([g5d/Cargo.toml](generation/g5d/Cargo.toml#L15)). Zero database queries in g5d.
- **g5-api contains no execution logic**: No `AgentLoop`, no LLM calls, no tool execution.
- **CRDT roles are correct**: g5-api is the Yjs authority (broadcast, persistence), g5d is a peer client (sync, materialize).
- **Results flow is clean**: g5d reports all results via `POST /api/internal/tasks/:id/transition`, checkpoints, timeline, usage, and file uploads.

### §24.1 — Draft commit should trigger on CRDT flush, not as a separate API call

**Current**: [draft_service.rs L640–L900](generation/g5-api/src/services/draft_service.rs#L640) performs a full write path (reconstruct `CrdtDoc` → materialize → git commit) as a user-initiated API call. This is synchronous and blocks the request thread.

**Proposed**: The draft commit becomes an automatic side-effect of CRDT flush/compaction. When the CRDT authority compacts its update log (already periodic in [crdt/persistence.rs](generation/g5-api/src/crdt/persistence.rs)), it atomically materializes and commits. No explicit "commit" API needed — the git history is a projection of CRDT state.

**Benefits**:
- Eliminates the user-facing commit API and its synchronous git I/O on request threads
- Git commits happen at CRDT compaction cadence (tunable), not on user action
- Naturally batches rapid edits into coherent commits
- g5-api's `repos/` volume access is scoped to this one well-defined write path

**Estimate**: 2 days (refactor commit into compaction hook + remove standalone commit endpoint)

### §24.2 — Job branch creation → g5d prepare phase

**Problem**: [job_service.rs L418–L440](generation/g5-api/src/services/job_service.rs#L418) calls `GitRepo::open` + `create_branch` when a job is created. This requires the API server to have write access beyond the commit-on-flush path.

**Proposed fix**: Branch creation becomes the first step of the job's first task (the existing "prepare" phase in g5d's [lifecycle.rs](generation/g5d/src/worker/lifecycle.rs)). g5-api records the desired branch name in the job metadata; g5d creates it on disk when the task starts.

**Estimate**: 1 day

### §24.3 — Job completion/rollback merge → g5d lifecycle step

**Problem**: [task_service.rs L1395–L1430](generation/g5-api/src/services/task_service.rs#L1395) performs `fast_forward_ref` to merge the job branch into the workspace base branch when all tasks complete. [job_service.rs L988–L1010](generation/g5-api/src/services/job_service.rs#L988) resets the branch on rollback.

**Proposed fix**: These become post-completion internal tasks. g5-api's state machine transitions the job to `merging` → dispatches a merge task to g5d → g5d performs the git ref manipulation → reports back → g5-api transitions to `merged`.

**Estimate**: 1 day

### §24.4 — Workspace merge → internal task

**Problem**: [workspace_service.rs L1728–L1790](generation/g5-api/src/services/workspace_service.rs#L1728) performs a `fast_forward_ref` merge directly.

**Proposed fix**: Same pattern as §24.3 — delegate to g5d as an internal task.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day

### §24.5 — Target architecture summary

After §24.1–§24.4, the boundary becomes:

| Component | Owns | Filesystem access |
|-----------|------|-------------------|
| **g5-api** | CRDT authority, commit-on-flush, local indexer (ontology reconciliation), SCM credential management (OAuth, token encryption, clone URLs, repo listing), doc-friendly interfaces, control plane (Postgres, WS broadcast, scheduling) | `repos/` — write-scoped to CRDT commit; read for indexer + comment context |
| **g5d** | Task execution, agent, remote repo sync (clone/fetch/rebase/push), branch management, merges, all other git writes | `repos/` — full read/write during task lifecycle |
| **g5-ui** | Presentation, CRDT peer (via g5-api WS), doc editing for non-engineers | None |

g5-api is the **workspace host for document-oriented users**: local indexer reconciles repo state → builds ontology → users edit specs/docs via CRDT → edits flush to git commits → indexer reconciles. The remote repo is an external connection synced by g5d. g5-api never contacts remote origins.

**Estimate**: 0.5 day (design doc finalizing the boundary)

### §24.6 — Repo refresh: g5-api triggering g5d sync tasks (DISCUSSION)

**Context**: [repo_fetcher.rs](generation/g5-api/src/maintenance/repo_fetcher.rs) currently runs inside g5-api as a background maintenance task, performing `git clone` and periodic `git fetch` against remote origins. Under the refined boundary, this network I/O moves to g5d — but g5-api still needs a mechanism to trigger repo refreshes automatically.

**Discussion — three candidate approaches:**

1. **Scheduled internal tasks**: g5-api creates periodic `repo_sync` internal tasks (e.g., every 5 minutes) that g5d picks up from the task queue. Reuses existing task infrastructure. Simple, but adds polling latency.

2. **Webhook-triggered tasks**: g5-api receives GitHub/GitLab webhooks (push events), then immediately enqueues a `repo_sync` task for g5d. Near-instant refresh on upstream changes. Requires webhook endpoint + secret management in g5-api (but no git operations — just task creation).

3. **Hybrid**: Webhook for push events (instant) + scheduled fallback (catches missed webhooks, repos without webhook support). This is the most robust.

**Open questions:**
- Should g5-api expose a manual "Refresh repo" button that enqueues a sync task? (Yes — useful for users who just pushed to origin.)
- Should the ontology reconciler run in g5-api (on local repo state) or also move to g5d? Keeping it in g5-api is simpler — it only reads the local repo and writes to Postgres, which are both g5-api's domain. The reconciler triggers after g5d reports a successful sync.
- Should g5d `POST /api/internal/repos/:id/synced` after fetch completes, so g5-api knows to reindex? (Yes — this closes the loop.)

**Proposed flow:**
```
Webhook/Schedule → g5-api enqueues repo_sync task
    → g5d picks up task, runs git fetch + rebase
    → g5d reports completion via POST /api/internal/repos/:id/synced
    → g5-api triggers ontology reconciler on local repo state
    → Ontology updated, UI reflects changes
```

**Estimate**: 1.5 days (repo_fetcher migration + sync task type + webhook endpoint)

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 24.1 | Commit-on-CRDT-flush (replace standalone commit API) | **HIGH** — simplifies write path | 2 days |
| 24.2 | Job branch creation → g5d prepare phase | MEDIUM — write coupling | 1 day |
| 24.3 | Job completion/rollback merge → g5d lifecycle | MEDIUM — write coupling | 1 day |
| 24.4 | Workspace merge → internal task | MEDIUM — write coupling | 0.5 day |
| 24.5 | Finalize boundary design doc | LOW — documentation | 0.5 day |
| 24.6 | Repo refresh mechanism (repo_fetcher → g5d + trigger) | MEDIUM — remote I/O in wrong component | 1.5 days |

**Total estimate**: ~6.5 days

## 25. Downlift Task DAG — Missing Inter-Task Dependencies

**Date added**: 2026-03-03
**Discovered during**: Demo seed of codex workspaces — all 170 downlift tasks run simultaneously with zero dependency edges.

### Problem

The downlift bootstrap ([bootstrap.rs L406–L443](generation/g5d/src/worker/bootstrap.rs#L406)) builds a dependency map by:
1. Converting each `file_path` from the `BootstrapScope` to a `component_id` via `IDService::file_to_component_id()`
2. Looking up the corresponding spec file at `.semlift/specs/{component_id}.semlift.md`
3. Parsing `dependencies:` from the spec's YAML frontmatter
4. Populating `depends_on` on each `TaskNodePayload`

The task scheduler ([task_service.rs L226–L248](generation/g5-api/src/services/task_service.rs#L226)) correctly enforces dependencies — a pending task is only eligible when all its `depends_on` entries are `completed`. The schema and enforcement are sound.

However, **two bugs cause the dependency map to always be empty**:

#### Bug 1: `file_path` → `component_id` prefix mismatch

The `BootstrapScope` is populated by a recursive CTE on `ontology_nodes` ([task_service.rs L527–L545](generation/g5-api/src/services/task_service.rs#L527)):

```sql
SELECT file_path FROM subtree WHERE file_path IS NOT NULL
```

This returns **all** `file_path` values in the ontology subtree, including:
- Code nodes: `codex_src/codex-rs/core/src/auth.rs` (repo-relative path with prefix)
- Spec nodes: `.semlift/specs/core/src/auth.semlift.md`

When `IDService::file_to_component_id()` processes a code node path like `codex_src/codex-rs/core/src/auth.rs`, it produces `codex_src/codex-rs/core/auth` (stripping `src/` prefix but keeping the repo-level prefix). The actual spec lives at `.semlift/specs/core/src/auth.semlift.md` (component_id = `core/src/auth`). The derived component_id doesn't match the spec path, so `read_to_string` returns `Err` and no dependencies are discovered.

#### Bug 2: Scope includes spec node `file_path` values

The scope query doesn't filter by `node_type`. Spec nodes have `file_path` values like `.semlift/specs/core/src/auth.semlift.md`. When `file_to_component_id()` processes these, it produces mangled IDs like `.semlift/specs/core/auth.semlift` — which don't correspond to any spec file on disk. These create junk tasks with no dependencies.

### Impact

All downlift tasks run with no ordering constraints. For leaf-level code tasks this is mostly harmless (each task operates on independent files). But for aggregate/module specs that should wait for their children, the lack of ordering means:
- Aggregate tasks may start before child tasks produce updated specs
- The LLM sees stale child specs when generating aggregate summaries
- Results are non-deterministic and potentially inconsistent

### Fix

#### Option A: Use `component_id` instead of `file_path` in scope query (recommended)

Change the `BootstrapScope` CTE to return `component_id` instead of (or alongside) `file_path`:

```sql
SELECT component_id, file_path
FROM subtree
WHERE file_path IS NOT NULL
  AND node_type = 'code'
```

The bootstrap then uses `component_id` directly as the key for spec lookup and dependency resolution, bypassing `file_to_component_id()` entirely. This requires:
1. Adding `component_id` to `BootstrapScope` (in `g5-common/types`)
2. Updating the scope CTE in `task_service.rs`
3. Updating `execute_downlift_bootstrap()` to use component_ids directly

#### Option B: Strip repo prefix before `file_to_component_id()` (workaround)

Have the bootstrap strip known repo prefixes (e.g., `codex_src/codex-rs/`) from file paths before calling `file_to_component_id()`. Fragile — depends on knowing the prefix convention per workspace.

#### Option C: Store canonical `component_id` on code nodes at seed time

Ensure the seed script stores the correct `component_id` on code ontology nodes (matching their parent spec's component_id-derived ID), and have the scope query return `component_id` instead of `file_path`. This is the clean long-term solution but requires schema/seed changes.

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 25.1 | Add `component_id` to `BootstrapScope` + update scope CTE | **HIGH** — downlift tasks run unordered | 0.5 day |
| 25.2 | Filter scope CTE to `node_type = 'code'` only | HIGH — junk tasks from spec nodes | 0.25 day |
| 25.3 | Update `execute_downlift_bootstrap()` to use component_ids directly | HIGH — dependency resolution broken | 0.5 day |
| 25.4 | Add integration test: downlift task graph has non-empty `depends_on` | MEDIUM — regression prevention | 0.5 day |

**Total estimate**: ~1.75 days

## 26. E2E Bootstrap Tests — Spec Fixtures Owned by Seed Script, Not the Tests

**Status**: Open  
**Severity**: LOW (test isolation / maintainability)  
**Introduced**: 2026-03-06

### Problem

`test_downlift_bootstrap_task_graph` and `test_uplift_bootstrap_task_graph` depend on spec files planted by `seed-e2e-workspace.sh` rather than setting up their own fixtures. This couples two tests to a shared infrastructure script also used by local dev setup.

- The **downlift test** requires `src_aggregate/main/lib` specs to exist so cascading downlift can read `child_spec_ids` (the LLM never runs in CI, so the agent never writes specs).
- The **uplift test** relies on those specs having `src_files: []` so the waterfall marks `main`/`lib` as `Modified` and `diff_to_task_graph`'s propagation logic promotes `src_aggregate` into the task graph.

Any change to the seed script's spec content can silently break one or both tests.

### Preferred Fix

Each test should write its own spec fixtures (e.g., via a `WorkerFixture::write_spec` helper) before creating the job, and clean them up afterwards. The seed script should own only source files and git initialisation, not spec state.

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 26.1 | Add `WorkerFixture::write_spec` / `delete_spec` helpers in `e2e/src/` | LOW | 0.5 day |
| 26.2 | Move spec seeding from seed script into `test_downlift_bootstrap_task_graph` setup | LOW | 0.25 day |
| 26.3 | Remove spec-seeding blocks from `seed-e2e-workspace.sh` | LOW | 0.25 day |

**Total estimate**: ~1 day

## 27. `ontology_nodes.file_path` Is Lossy — Should Be `src_files TEXT[]`

**Status**: Open  
**Severity**: MEDIUM (data correctness)  
**Introduced**: 2026-03-06

### Problem

The `ontology_nodes` table stores source file associations as `file_path TEXT` (singular, nullable). When the uplift bootstrap upserts ontology nodes, it truncates the full `src_files` array to `src_files.first().cloned()`:

```rust
// g5-api/src/routes/internal.rs (upsert handler)
let file_path = node.src_files.first().cloned();
```

This means:
- Multi-file components (e.g. a spec covering `["src/main.rs", "src/utils.rs"]`) lose all but the first file
- `BootstrapScope.file_paths` (built from `ontology_nodes.file_path`) is incomplete for multi-file specs
- Scoped uplift and downlift may miss files that belong to the target subtree

The full `src_files` array is preserved on the `tasks` table (`TEXT[]`), but the ontology — the long-lived structural record — is lossy.

### Preferred Fix

| # | Item | Severity | Estimate |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 27.1 | Add migration: `ALTER TABLE ontology_nodes ADD COLUMN src_files TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'; UPDATE ontology_nodes SET src_files = CASE WHEN file_path IS NOT NULL THEN ARRAY[file_path] ELSE '{}' END;` | MEDIUM | 0.25 day |
| 27.2 | Update upsert handler in `internal.rs` to store full `node.src_files` in `src_files` column | MEDIUM | 0.25 day |
| 27.3 | Update `BootstrapScope` construction in `task_service.rs` to use `src_files` array instead of scalar `file_path` | MEDIUM | 0.5 day |
| 27.4 | Keep `file_path` column as computed/derived for backward compat or drop it | LOW | 0.25 day |

**Total estimate**: ~1.25 days

## 29. AlloyDB Serverless — Cloud SQL Replacement for Scale-to-Zero

**Status**: Open (investigation)  
**Severity**: LOW (cost optimization)  
**Introduced**: 2026-03-07

### Motivation

Cloud SQL has no native scale-to-zero. The dev instance runs 24/7 (~$200/mo) even when idle. AlloyDB Serverless auto-pauses compute after idle timeout (default 10 min) and resumes on connection — true scale-to-zero with ~$50-150/mo savings in dev.

### Compatibility Audit

All PostgreSQL features used by G5 are supported by AlloyDB:

| Feature | G5 Usage | AlloyDB |
|---------|----------|---------|
| pgvector (HNSW, `vector(1536)`) | Semantic search embeddings | ✅ Native (AlloyDB has optimized pgvector) |
| Row-Level Security (21 tables) | Multi-tenant org isolation | ✅ |
| SECURITY DEFINER functions | `authz.set_ctx/clear_ctx/current_org_ids` | ✅ |
| Custom NOLOGIN roles | `g5_tenant`, `g5_app`, `authz_writer`, `authz_ctx_writer` | ✅ |
| `SET ROLE` / role inheritance | Per-connection role switching | ✅ |
| `pg_backend_pid()` session context | `authz.session_ctx` keyed by PID | ✅ |
| Triggers (20+ BEFORE INSERT) | Auto-set `org_id` from session | ✅ |
| JSONB, UUID[], TEXT[] | Metadata, scopes, org_ids | ✅ |
| GIN indexes (full-text search) | `tsvector` on search_documents, chat_sessions | ✅ |
| CMEK encryption | KMS-managed keys | ✅ |
| Private IP / VPC | No public endpoint | ✅ |
| sqlx (runtime-tokio + rustls, native roots) | Direct connection pool, no PgBouncer | ✅ |

### Version Constraint

G5 currently uses **PostgreSQL 17**. AlloyDB version support must be verified at migration time — PG 14/15 was initially supported, PG 16+ likely available by now. If PG 17 is not yet supported, a version downgrade is required (test all 27 migrations against the target PG version first).

### Non-Portable Patterns (require changes)

| Pattern | Current (Cloud SQL) | AlloyDB Equivalent |
|---------|--------------------|--------------------|
| `cloudsqlsuperuser` role membership | Auto-granted to `google_sql_user` resources | Manual `GRANT` via bootstrap SQL or AlloyDB IAM auth |
| `google_sql_user` Terraform resource | Creates Cloud SQL users | `google_alloydb_user` or SQL-based user provisioning |
| `google_sql_database_instance` | Cloud SQL instance config | `google_alloydb_cluster` + `google_alloydb_instance` |
| Cloud SQL Auth Proxy | Optional (G5 uses direct private IP) | AlloyDB Auth Proxy available (same pattern) |
| `ssl_mode = "ENCRYPTED_ONLY"` | Cloud SQL setting | AlloyDB enforces TLS by default |

### AlloyDB Serverless Benefits

- **Scale-to-zero**: Auto-pause after idle timeout, resume on connection (~3-5s cold start)
- **Faster pgvector**: AlloyDB has Google-optimized vector indexing (up to 10x faster ANN queries)
- **Columnar engine**: Automatic columnar caching for analytical queries (free, no config)
- **Per-second billing**: Pay only for compute seconds used (vs. Cloud SQL's per-hour minimum)

### Migration Estimate

| # | Item | Effort | Notes |
|---|------|--------|-------|
| 29.1 | Verify AlloyDB PG version support, benchmark pgvector perf | 0.5 day | Check if PG 17 supported; if not, test PG 15/16 compat |
| 29.2 | Create AlloyDB Terraform module (`google_alloydb_cluster` + `google_alloydb_instance`) | 1 day | Replace `modules/cloudsql/`, update variables |
| 29.3 | Migrate user provisioning from `google_sql_user` to SQL bootstrap | 0.5 day | `g5`, `g5_admin`, `authz_writer`, `authz_ctx_writer` |
| 29.4 | Update ESO template for AlloyDB connection string | 0.25 day | Same format, different host IP |
| 29.5 | Data migration via `pg_dump` / `pg_restore` | 0.5 day | Downtime window required |
| 29.6 | Validate all 27 migrations + RLS + pgvector against AlloyDB | 1 day | E2E test suite |
| 29.7 | Update docker-compose dev to match target PG version if needed | 0.25 day | Change `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` base image |

**Total estimate**: ~4 days  
**Priority**: P3 (cost optimization, not blocking)

## 30. Non-Superuser Runtime App User

**Status**: ⚠️ PARTIALLY FIXED (implemented in this branch; rollout/rotation follow-through still required)  
**Severity**: HIGH (security)  
**Introduced**: 2026-03-07

### Problem

This debt originally came from running the application on the Terraform-created
`g5` Cloud SQL login everywhere. That login receives `cloudsqlsuperuser`, which
includes `CREATEROLE`, broad grant power, and practical bypass of the role
hierarchy we intended for runtime separation.

This means:
- SQL injection through the app can escalate to full database control
- The app can modify RLS policies, drop schemas, or create new users
- The carefully designed NOLOGIN role hierarchy (`g5_tenant`, `g5_app`, `authz_writer`, `authz_ctx_writer`) provides no security boundary when the connecting user is a superuser

The migration user needs superuser privileges (`ALTER FUNCTION OWNER`, `GRANT`
across roles). The app runtime does not.

### Current status in this branch

The branch now has a real runtime split and parity lane:

- SQL/bootstrap creates restricted runtime identities via
  `scripts/bootstrap-runtime-db-users.sh`
- app startup supports strict runtime split enforcement via
  `G5_REQUIRE_RUNTIME_DB_SPLIT`
- local Docker CI and Cloud Build now bootstrap distinct runtime users before
  the app starts
- local `just ci-docker` passes end-to-end under the least-privilege split
  instead of collapsing back to the admin login

What remains is rollout and operational cleanup: cloud environments must run on
the split runtime users everywhere, and secret rotation/deployment follow-through
must be treated as part of closing the debt.

### Approach

Since `google_sql_user` always grants `cloudsqlsuperuser`, restricted runtime
users must be created via SQL bootstrap rather than Terraform-managed Cloud SQL
users. The migration/bootstrap path is the right place because it already runs
with the admin `g5` identity.

**Migration user**: `g5` (Terraform `google_sql_user`, cloudsqlsuperuser) — runs migrations only  
**Runtime users**:

- `g5_runtime_system` — system/app pool runtime identity
- `g5_runtime_tenant` — tenant pool runtime identity subject to RLS

The runtime users inherit only the roles they actually need and can call the
authz helpers they need, but cannot:
- `CREATE ROLE`, `ALTER ROLE`, or `DROP ROLE`
- `ALTER FUNCTION OWNER`
- Modify RLS policies
- Access tables not explicitly granted

### Implementation

| # | Item | Status | Notes |
|---|------|--------|-------|
| 30.1 | Bootstrap restricted runtime DB users and passwords | ✅ FIXED IN BRANCH | `scripts/bootstrap-runtime-db-users.sh` now creates split runtime identities instead of relying on the admin login at runtime. |
| 30.2 | Wire CI/local runtime URLs and strict split enforcement | ✅ FIXED IN BRANCH | `docker/docker-compose.test.yml`, `cloudbuild-ci.yaml`, `g5-api/src/config.rs`, and test harness wiring now run under the split DB credentials with `G5_REQUIRE_RUNTIME_DB_SPLIT`. |
| 30.3 | Wire dev/staging/prod manifests and secret templates for split runtime URLs | ✅ FIXED IN BRANCH | Infra/Helm/ESO templates now carry the split runtime DB secret shape; rendered manifests were verified locally. |
| 30.4 | Roll out, rotate, and verify cloud environments on the split runtime identities | ⬜ | Remaining operational step: complete environment rollout, confirm runtime no longer falls back to `g5`, and treat any previously exposed/shared credentials as rotation work. |

**Remaining work**:

- complete cloud rollout verification in dev/staging/prod
- keep `g5` admin-only in real runtime, not just CI/local
- preserve CI parity so future request-path regressions are caught under the
  least-privilege credential model

## 32. Customizable Skills & Subagents — Enterprise Agent Extension Framework

**Status**: Not started
